title: Leokani G2P custom pronunciations (user lexicon), v1.1
description: Shared by every port (Python, C, JS/WASM, Swift). Semantics, identical in every port: (1) APPLIED BEFORE LOOKUP, in the normaliser's per-token step, before any normaliser rule: the token is split into lead/core/trail exactly as Normalizer.split does, and only the core is matched; lead and trail punctuation are kept. (2) CASE: a key with no uppercase letter matches the core in any casing; a key with an uppercase letter matches only that exact casing. An exact-case key wins over a lowercase key. (3) POSSESSIVE: if no entry matches the core and the core ends in 's or ’s (or s' / s’), the stem (without 's, or without the final apostrophe) is matched; a phoneme entry then gets the suffix appended (stem ends, ignoring ˈ ˌ, in s z ʃ ʒ ʧ ʤ -> ᵻz; in p t k f θ -> s; else z; a plural possessive s' / s’ adds nothing), a respelling entry gets 's appended to its last word. (4) A PHONEME entry becomes the word's base (as SAY_AS does: core + U+E000 + phonemes), so the context model still places it in the clause; its phonemes must use only the release's symbols (outSymbols, ˈ, ˌ, and space between parts). (5) A RESPELLING entry replaces the core with the respelling's words, which then go through the normaliser, lexicon and letter-to-sound model as written text. (6) Keys are single tokens: no whitespace; letters, digits, apostrophes, hyphens and periods allowed. Later entries replace earlier ones with the same key. An empty user lexicon changes nothing: goldens.json still reproduces exactly. Loaders: JSON (this schema) and TSV (one entry per line: key TAB value; a value written /like this/ is phonemes, otherwise a respelling; blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped). In JSON, a bare string value follows the same slash rule; an object value names its kind explicitly.
